text: Nisbett and Wilson's "Telling More Than We Can Know" (1977) is standardly cited to support which claim about introspection?
choices: People often accurately report the OUTPUT of a cognitive process while being unaware of, and confabulating, its actual causes
Introspection gives incorrigible access to the causes of our choices
Sufficient introspective training can eliminate all reporting error
explanation: They showed that subjects confabulate reasons -- citing influences that demonstrably had no effect and missing ones that did -- so introspective access to the causes of behavior is unreliable, even though people can report a process's conclusion. Option B is the classical view it refutes, C overstates neurophenomenology's ambitions, and D is an eliminativist thesis they do not argue.
